html:
The Huaihai campaign was fought from 6 November 1948 to 10 January 1949 around the city of Xuzhou in eastern China, north of the Huai River. The Communist army destroyed the main Nationalist forces north of the Yangtze, which decided the Chinese Civil War.

By late 1948 the Communists had won Manchuria. The Nationalists of Chiang Kai-shek massed about 800,000 men at Xuzhou, a railway junction that guarded the road to their capital, Nanjing. About 600,000 Communist regulars moved against them, led by a committee that included Deng Xiaoping and supplied by millions of peasants. They did not attack the city. They cut off and surrounded the Nationalist armies one at a time: first an army east of Xuzhou, then one sent to relieve it, and last the main force as it tried to pull out. Some Nationalist units changed sides, and Communist spies sat in Chiang's headquarters.

The Nationalists lost about 550,000 men, most of them captured or gone over to the enemy. Chiang stepped down as president in January. In April the Communists crossed the Yangtze and took Nanjing, and on 1 October Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic. The Nationalists retreated to Taiwan.
